proposals.evidence: CDIAL 142 accha gives Punjabi acchā “good”, explicitly borrowed into standard Hindi, and Old Marwari āchyo/āchī. The route is decided locally: standard Hindi is linked to the existing Punjabi attestation; direct western āch- continuations are kept separate from unresolved regional contact forms.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5731.1 tala explicitly includes adverbial Nepali tala, Bengali/Assamese tale, Bhojpuri tar and Hindi tar/tare/tale “below”. This is the base/bottom noun used as an adverb; doubled-l forms that may select *talla are not included.
